Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, homogeneous, well-circumscribed opacity in the right hemithorax that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall, a classic radiographic sign of an extrapulmonary (pleural-based) mass rather than an intrapulmonary lesion. This is confirmed by the CT images (Figures 2 and 3), which show a distinct pleural mass compressing the lung parenchyma.
